title: What did you do?
goal: Say what you did with the passé composé (avoir + a participle in -é), and ask a colleague about their weekend.

items.en: passé composé with avoir (I worked, I have worked)

accept: Ils ont appelé leur mère.
Ils ont téléphoné à leur mère.
drills.explain: ils → ont + appelé. Appeler keeps one l in the participle.

drills.prompt: How do you say “I ate at the restaurant”?
drills.explain: You need both parts: avoir (j'ai) + the participle with é (mangé).
voyager → voyagé: the e after g is not needed before é.

items.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu as fait en fin de semaine ?
items.en: What did you do on the weekend? (to a friend)

items.note: fait is the participle of faire. You will learn it properly in the next lesson; for now, learn the question as a chunk.

blocks.title: By the coffee machine, Monday 9 a.m.
blocks.context: Raj and Camille work for a small software company in Montréal. Amira, a new colleague, joins them.

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Salut Raj ! Ça va ? Qu'est-ce que tu as fait en fin de semaine ?
lines.en: Hi Raj! How are you? What did you do on the weekend?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Ça va bien, merci. Samedi matin, j'ai travaillé un peu, et l'après-midi, j'ai rangé mon appartement.
lines.en: Fine, thanks. On Saturday morning I worked a bit, and in the afternoon I tidied my apartment.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Non, mais le soir, j'ai invité des amis. On a mangé une poutine et on a regardé le match des Canadiens.
lines.en: No, but in the evening I invited some friends over. We ate poutine and watched the Canadiens game.

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Ah oui ! Ils ont gagné, non ?
lines.en: Oh yes! They won, didn't they?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Oui, quatre à deux ! Et toi ?

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Moi, dimanche, nous avons fêté l'anniversaire de ma sœur. Mes parents et moi, nous avons préparé un gros brunch pour toute la famille.
lines.en: Me, on Sunday we celebrated my sister's birthday. My parents and I made a big brunch for the whole family.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Bonjour ! Vous parlez de la fin de semaine ? Moi, j'ai passé une très belle fin de semaine. J'ai rencontré mes nouveaux voisins, et on a joué aux cartes jusqu'à minuit !
lines.en: Hello! Are you talking about the weekend? I had a really nice weekend. I met my new neighbours, and we played cards until midnight!

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Super ! Bienvenue dans le quartier, alors.
lines.en: Great! Welcome to the neighbourhood, then.

blocks.body: Listen first. Many verbs here are about the past: [[j'ai travaillé]], [[j'ai rangé]], [[on a mangé]]. Can you spot the two parts in each one?

blocks.prompt: What did Raj do on Saturday evening?
options: He had friends over, ate poutine and watched hockey
He went to a birthday brunch
blocks.explain: [[J'ai invité des amis. On a mangé une poutine et on a regardé le match.]] He tidied his apartment in the afternoon.

blocks.title: Two parts: avoir + participle
blocks.body:
To say what you **did** (a finished action), French uses the **passé composé**, a “compound past”. It has **two parts**:

- the verb **avoir** in the present: [[j'ai, tu as, il a…]] (you already know it)
- the **past participle** of the main verb: [[travaillé, mangé, regardé]]

So [[j'ai travaillé]] is literally “I have worked”, but it covers all of these in English: *I worked, I have worked, I did work*. One French form, three English ones.

blocks.title: Regarder in the passé composé
head: avoir
participle
English
blocks.note: Only **avoir** changes. The participle [[regardé]] stays the same for every person. Watch the liaison: [[nous‿avons]], [[vous‿avez]], [[ils‿ont]], [[elles‿ont]] all link with a *z* sound.

blocks.title: Making the participle of an -er verb
blocks.note: Every **-er** verb (the biggest verb family) follows the same rule: take off **-er**, add **-é**. Spelling changes from the present disappear: [[appeler → appelé]] (one l), [[commencer → commencé]] (no ç), [[manger → mangé]] (no extra e).

examples.fr: Nous avons commencé à neuf heures.
On a joué au soccer dimanche.

blocks.title: Why “j'ai mangé” can mean “I ate” and “I have eaten”
blocks.body:
English has two past forms: *I ate yesterday* (simple past) and *I have eaten already* (present perfect). Spoken French uses the **passé composé** for both.

- [[Hier, j'ai mangé une poutine.]] = Yesterday I **ate** a poutine.
- [[J'ai déjà mangé.]] = I **have** already **eaten**.

So don't look for a “did” in French questions: [[Tu as mangé ?]] = *Did you eat?* / *Have you eaten?*

blocks.title: Je mange or j'ai mangé?
blocks.body:
This is the most important sound difference in this unit:

- [[je mange]] (present): *je* sounds like *zhuh*
- [[j'ai mangé]] (past): *j'ai* sounds like *zhay*, and there is a second *é* at the end

Also, [[mangé]], [[manger]] and [[mangez]] all sound **exactly the same**. When you hear avoir before it, write **-é**: [[j'ai mangé]]. When you hear another verb before it, write the infinitive: [[je vais manger]].

- **Forgetting avoir:** [[Je mangé]] is wrong. You always need both parts: [[J'ai mangé]].
- **Infinitive instead of participle:** [[J'ai manger]] sounds right but is spelled wrong. After avoir: **-é**.
- **Using être:** [[Je suis mangé]] means “I am eaten”! Most verbs use avoir. (A small group uses être; that is Unit 2.)
- **Translating “did”:** there is no extra word for *did*. “Did you eat?” is simply [[Tu as mangé ?]]
- **Forgetting élision:** [[je ai]] → [[j'ai]].

blocks.title: Weekend talk in Québec
blocks.body:
On Monday at work in Québec, you will hear [[Pis, ta fin de semaine ?]] (So, how was your weekend? *Pis* is a very informal spoken form of *puis*, “and then / so”). In France, people say [[le week-end]]; in Québec, [[la fin de semaine]] is standard, though [[le weekend]] is also heard.

In speech, [[on a…]] is much more common than [[nous avons…]]: [[On a mangé une poutine]]. Both mean *we*. Use **nous** in formal writing.

The hockey team is [[le Canadien de Montréal]], and fans talk about [[les Canadiens]] or *the Habs*.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Say each line out loud. Feel the two parts: avoir, then the participle.

lines.tip: j'ai = zhay; travaillé ends in a clear é.
Rising voice at the end for a question.
on a: the n links to a: o-na.

lines.fr: Nous avons fêté l'anniversaire de ma sœur.
Ils ont gagné quatre à deux.
lines.tip: Link: il-zont. Without the z it would be ils sont (they are).

blocks.prompt: Is this about now or about the past?
blocks.explain: You heard [[j'ai]] (zhay) + [[parlé]]: avoir + participle = passé composé. The present would be [[je parle]].

options: They are going to watch a movie.
blocks.explain: [[ils‿ont]] with a *z* sound + [[regardé]]: past. The future would be [[ils vont regarder]].

blocks.prompt: Is this about now or about the past?
blocks.explain: [[je]] (zhuh) and no second part: present tense. The past would be [[j'ai mangé avec Amira]].

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Answer without scrolling back. Two parts every time: avoir + participle.

blocks.text: Samedi, j'___ travaillé et nous ___ regardé un film.
blocks.en: On Saturday, I worked and we watched a movie.
blocks.explain: j' → ai, nous → avons. The participle never changes.
appeler → appelé, with one l (the double l of j'appelle is only in the present).

optionFeedback: That is the present: we visit / we are visiting.
That is the futur proche: we are going to visit.
After avoir, use the participle with é: visité.

blocks.prompt: I ate at the restaurant with Raj.
accept: J'ai mangé au restaurant avec Raj.
J'ai mangé dans un restaurant avec Raj.
blocks.explain: manger → mangé. In English it's “ate”, in French [[j'ai mangé]].

blocks.prompt: Match each infinitive with its participle.
What did you do on the weekend? (to a friend)
accept: Qu'est-ce que tu as fait en fin de semaine ?
En fin de semaine, qu'est-ce que tu as fait ?

blocks.prompt: They (women) celebrated Sofia's birthday on Sunday.
accept: Elles ont fêté l'anniversaire de Sofia dimanche.
Dimanche, elles ont fêté l'anniversaire de Sofia.
blocks.explain: elles → ont + fêté. Days take no preposition: [[dimanche]] = on Sunday.
vous → [[avez]], and gagné ends in é. Hear the link: vou-zavez.

blocks.text: Demain, je vais ___ ma mère. Hier, j'ai ___ mon père. (appeler)
blocks.en: Tomorrow I'm going to call my mother. Yesterday I called my father.
blocks.explain: After aller (future), keep the infinitive: [[appeler]]. After avoir (past), use the participle: [[appelé]]. They sound the same!

blocks.prompt: It's Monday morning. A colleague asks what you did on the weekend. Answer with three things you did (use -er verbs), then ask the question back.
checklist: Three verbs in the passé composé with avoir
At least one with on a or nous avons
The question back: Et toi, qu'est-ce que tu as fait ?

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Samedi, j'ai travaillé le matin. L'après-midi, j'ai acheté un manteau au centre-ville. Dimanche, j'ai invité des amis et on a mangé une raclette. Et toi, qu'est-ce que tu as fait ?
models.en: On Saturday I worked in the morning. In the afternoon I bought a coat downtown. On Sunday I invited some friends and we ate raclette. And you, what did you do?

blocks.prompt: Write a short message to a friend about your weekend: four sentences in the passé composé with avoir, using four different -er verbs.
checklist: Four different -er verbs with the participle in -é
avoir conjugated correctly (j'ai, on a, nous avons…)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Karim ! J'ai passé une belle fin de semaine. Samedi, j'ai joué au soccer avec mes collègues et on a gagné ! Dimanche, j'ai rangé mon appartement et j'ai téléphoné à mes parents. À bientôt, Nguyen
models.en: Hi Karim! I had a nice weekend. On Saturday I played soccer with my colleagues and we won! On Sunday I tidied my apartment and called my parents. See you soon, Nguyen

summary:
- Form the **passé composé** with avoir: [[j'ai, tu as, il a, nous avons, vous avez, ils ont]] + participle
- Make the participle of any **-er** verb: [[parler → parlé]]
- Hear the difference between [[je mange]] and [[j'ai mangé]]
- Ask [[Qu'est-ce que tu as fait en fin de semaine ?]] and answer in three sentences
